Once upon a time there was a woman who wanted to paint something special. She was very persistent and worked hard every day. She painted and painted until one day she was almost done. But then, there was a problem. 

The woman was out of paint and was getting very frustrated. She didn't know what to do. Suddenly, a little voice said, "I can help!"

The woman looked down and saw a three-year-old boy smiling up at her. He had a bright blue paintbrush in his hand. The woman asked the boy, "Where did you get that brush?".

The boy replied, "I can help you paint. I was very persistent and I asked my mommy." The woman smiled and thanked the boy. They worked together and soon the painting was finished. 

The woman was very happy with her new painting. She thanked the little boy for being so persistent and helping her to finish it. They both admired their work and the painting hung proudly in the woman's home.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate jail. It was a special place that kept people safe. But one day, the jail would not open. No matter how hard the people tried, they could not unlock it. 

Then a brave little boy came along. He had a secret plan. He knew just how to unlock the delicate jail. Everyone watched him in awe as he carefully worked his magic.

He used his special key to unlock the jail. A giant cheer went up as the door opened. Everyone was happy to be free and ran off to play. The little boy had unlocked the delicate jail!

Ben loves to play with his toy cars and trucks. He has a big red fire truck with a loud engine and a long ladder. He likes to pretend he is a fireman and save people from fires.

One day, he is playing with his fire truck in the living room. He makes the engine sound with his mouth and moves the ladder up and down. He sees his mom sitting on the couch with a book. He thinks she is bored and wants to play with him.

"Mom, mom, look at my fire truck!" he says, driving the truck towards her. "It has a big engine and a long ladder. Do you want to see?"

Mom smiles and puts down her book. She is happy that Ben is having fun, but she also wants him to be careful. She knows the fire truck is heavy and can hurt someone if it hits them.

"Sure, Ben, I want to see your fire truck. But be gentle, okay? Don't make it go too fast or too hard. You might break something or hurt someone."

Ben nods, but he is too excited to listen. He wants to show his mom how fast and strong his fire truck is. He makes the engine sound louder and pushes the truck harder. He does not see the coffee table in front of him.

Crash! The fire truck hits the coffee table and knocks over a vase. The vase falls to the floor and breaks into pieces. Water and flowers spill everywhere. The living room is a messy mess.

Mom gasps and jumps up from the couch. She is angry and scared. She sees the broken vase and the wet carpet. She sees Ben and his fire truck.

"Ben, what did you do?" she says, raising her voice. "You made a big mess. You broke the vase. You did not listen to me. You were not gentle. You were very naughty."

Ben feels a hot feeling in his face. He is sorry and sad. He did not mean to break the vase or make a mess. He just wanted to play with his fire truck and make his mom happy. He looks at his mom and sees her angry face. He feels embarrassed.

"I'm sorry, mom," he says, in a small voice. "I did not see the table. I did not want to break the vase. I wanted to show you my fire truck. I like my fire truck. It has a big engine and a long ladder."

Mom sighs and kneels down next to Ben. She is still angry, but she also loves him. She knows he is a good boy, but he needs to learn to be careful and respectful.

"I know you like your fire truck, Ben. And I like to see you play with it. But you have to be careful and listen to me. You have to be gentle and not make a mess. You have to say sorry when you do something wrong. Do you understand?"

Ben nods and hugs his mom. He is still sorry and sad, but he also feels better. He knows his mom loves him and wants him to be good.

"I understand, mom. I'm sorry. I love you."

Mom hugs him back and kisses his cheek. She loves him too.

"I love you too, Ben. Now, let's clean up this mess together, okay?"

Ben agrees and helps his mom pick up the broken vase and the wet flowers. He puts his fire truck away and says goodbye to it. He learns his lesson and promises to be more careful and gentle next time. He and his mom are happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little cube. One day, the lonely cube wanted to jump around so he decided to try it out. He jumped up, up, and up!

Suddenly, the cube heard a voice. He looked around and then saw a little girl. She smiled and said "Hello cube! My name is Susan. Would you like to play?" 

The cube was so excited and he nodded his little block head. "Yes, I would love to play!"

The cube and little Susan played all day. They jumped and jumped and jumped. But soon, the sun began to set and it was time for Susan to go home. 

The cube waved goodbye to Susan and said "Come back soon!" And then the poor little cube jumped up in the air, feeling happy and content.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, named Brandy and Kris. They loved to play together. One day, they decided to have a game of hide and seek. Brandy was the seeker. She closed her eyes and counted to ten while Kris quickly found a hiding spot behind the purple sofa.

When Brandy was done counting, she looked around but couldn't find her friend. Suddenly, she heard a giggle in the corner. She looked to the sofa and saw a pair of purple shoes sticking out! She knew it was Kris.

She started to walk over to grab Kris, but something caught her attention. There was a small purple player laying on the floor. She had never seen that before. Brandy absent-mindedly picked up the player before she continued to go after Kris.

But it was too late! She had slipped up and Kris heard her. Kris jumped out from behind the sofa and ran away. Brandy chased her for a bit before giving up. She returned to the purple player and decided to take it home with her. From then on, she and Kris always loved playing with the purple player.

Once upon a time there was a puppy with a sweet, scruffy fur collar. He had four furry paws and always wanted to go faster and faster. One day, he chased a rabbit and ran so fast that his collar flew off and he lost it. He whined sadly, he wanted his collar back.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was the rabbit! He had found the collar and put it around his neck. "It's all right, I found it again," the rabbit said. The puppy was so happy, he gave the rabbit a big wet lick on the nose and ran around in circles! They ran faster and faster, the rabbit holding on to the collar so it wouldn't disappear again.

The rabbit and puppy became best friends, running and playing together all the time. Whenever the puppy went a little too fast and the collar began to slide off, the rabbit was always there to put it back around his neck. His sweet, scruffy fur collar stayed with him forever.

One day, a little bird named Tim wanted to fly high in the sky. He saw a tall pole and thought it would be fun to fly to the top. So, Tim flapped his wings and flew up, up, up!

When Tim reached the top of the pole, he found a hidden nest. In the nest, there was another little bird named Sue. Sue looked at Tim and said, "Hi! I did not think anyone would find my hidden nest!"

Tim said, "I like to fly high! I saw your pole and wanted to see what was at the top." They both became friends and had fun flying and playing together. They would fly high in the sky and then come back to their hidden nest on the tall pole.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy boy. He was very mean and loved to tease the other children. One day, he was playing with a shiny pin. He went to the park to find someone to tease.

He soon found a little girl, who was only three. The boy thought it would be fun to tease her with the pin. He showed the girl the pin, and she was so excited. She started to laugh and smile.

But then, the wealthy boy teasing her with the pin got too close. He accidentally poked the little girl with the pin! Ouch! The girl started to cry. She had never felt such pain.

The wealthy boy was scared. He ran away from the park, leaving the little girl all alone. He did not apologize or even look back. 

The little girl was so sad and scared. She had never been teased like that before. She never wanted to see the wealthy boy again. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she met a humble old man who owned a small garden.

"Hello, little girl," said the old man. "What brings you here?"

"I like to see the world," replied Lily. "What do you own?"

"I own this garden," said the old man. "It's not much, but it's mine."

Lily looked around the garden and saw all the beautiful flowers and vegetables. "It's so pretty," she said. "Can I help you take care of it?"

The old man smiled and said, "That would be wonderful. Together, we can make the world a more beautiful place." And from that day on, Lily visited the old man's garden every day to help him take care of it. They became good friends and learned that even the smallest things can make a big difference in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She lived in a big jungle with many animals. One day, Lily saw a leopard who was hurt. She wanted to help the leopard, so she managed to get close to him and give him some food. 

The leopard was happy and grateful to Lily. They became friends and played together every day. But one day, the leopard got scared and attacked Lily. She was hurt badly and couldn't move. 

Lily cried out for help, but no one came. The leopard felt sorry, but it was too late. Lily's kindness had led her to a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they played catch with a ball. Tim caught the ball and felt very happy.

Tim's mommy and daddy were getting married soon. Tim was nervous about the big day. He didn't know what to wear or what to say. But his mommy and daddy said they loved him no matter what.

On the day of the marriage, Tim wore a nice suit and stood next to his mommy and daddy. He was still nervous, but he felt happy too. When his mommy and daddy said "I do," Tim caught a flower that the bride threw. He smiled and felt proud to be a part of the special day.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit. The rabbit was very popular because he was very cute. Everyone loved the rabbit and wanted to be his friend. One day, the rabbit's friend wanted to send him a letter. The friend wrote a letter and put it in an envelope. Then, the friend sent the letter to the rabbit's house. The rabbit was very happy when he got the letter. He hopped around and showed it to all his friends. From that day on, the rabbit's friend sent him letters all the time. The rabbit was very happy and felt even more popular. The end.

Once upon a time there was a wild place. It was very unique, like somewhere you had never seen before. One day a little boy wanted to spend some time there. He wanted to explore and see all the beautiful things.

So the little boy set off on his adventure. He had lots of fun looking at the amazing flowers and plants. And he was so excited to see all the animals! But soon he started to get tired, so he decided to stop and rest.

Unfortunately, when the little boy finally woke up from his nap, he realised he was lost. He had no idea which way to go. He started to cry and he said, "Where am I?"

The little boy tried and tried to find his way back, but he couldn't. He was stuck in the wild place forever!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Thomas. He was three years old and loved playing with his toys. Every day, his mom would put a belt on him before they went outside. Thomas didn't like wearing his belt - he would always complain to his mom.

One day, Thomas put on his belt and started to complain even louder. His mom didn't want to listen, so she tied the belt extra tight. She said, "Come on, Thomas, we need to go outside now!" But Thomas was feeling miserable because of his belt. He just wanted to stay inside and play with his toys.

Thomas's mom said, "Thomas, you have to wear the belt or you can't go outside". Thomas had no choice but to wear it. Grumpily, he followed his mom outside and started playing. Even though he was wearing his belt, Thomas still had fun playing with his friends.

At the end of the day, Thomas's mom untied his belt after he came back inside. Thomas felt much better and instantly forgot about his belt troubles. He filled his mom in on all the fun he had outside and she was glad that he was no longer complaining.

Once upon a time, there lived a purple monster. He lived in a far away forest and was lonely - he had no friends. One day, the purple monster had a special delivery. When he opened the box he found a magical purple ball. 

He was so excited and decided to show his new toy to the world. He called his new friends - the birds, the squirrels and the foxes â€“ to come and play. They all had lots of fun bouncing and throwing the ball.

They even made up a game called â€˜Deliveryâ€™. They took it in turns delivering the ball to each other. When the sun went down, the purple monster had made lots of new friends. He was so happy and never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Sally. They loved to play together and have lots of fun. One day, they decided to have a race to see who could run the fastest. It was a very competitive race, and they both wanted to win.

As they were running, Timmy started to get tired and wanted to stop. Sally noticed this and decided to slow down a bit so that they could finish the race together. When they finally reached the finish line, they were both very happy and had lots of fun.

After the race, they decided to go to the park and play on the swings. When it was time to go home, Sally said goodbye to Timmy and gave him a big hug. Timmy smiled and closed his eyes, feeling happy to have such a good friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play in the garden and eat carrots. One day, while Fluffy was playing, he saw a big hole in the fence. Fluffy wanted to escape and explore the world outside the garden.

Fluffy went to his friend, a little bird named Tweety. "Tweety, I want to escape and see the world outside the garden. Do you want to come with me?" asked Fluffy. "Yes, I want to come with you," replied Tweety.

Fluffy and Tweety went through the hole in the fence and started to explore. They saw a big tree and decided to climb it. While they were climbing, Fluffy's nail got stuck in the tree. "Oh no, my nail is stuck!" cried Fluffy. Tweety helped Fluffy free his nail.

After a while, they saw a cheap ice cream truck. They went to the truck and bought some ice cream. Fluffy and Tweety had a great adventure and couldn't wait to explore more of the world outside the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his ball. One day, Timmy went to play outside and his ball rolled away from him. Timmy tried to get his ball back, but it rolled down a big hill and into a well.

Timmy was sad because he thought he would never see his ball again. But then, Timmy remembered something his mommy told him. She said, "If something is hard to do, just take it easy and don't give up."

So, Timmy took a deep breath and went to get his ball. He climbed down into the well and rolled the ball back up to the top. Timmy was so happy that he didn't give up and got his ball back. From that day on, Timmy remembered to take it easy and never give up when things get hard.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little mouse named Max. Max lived in a cozy hole in the wall of a big house. One day, Max saw a big cat outside his hole. "Oh no!" cried Max. "I need to move fast!"

Max ran in motion to find a new home. He saw a friendly rabbit and asked, "Do you know where I can find a new home?" The rabbit replied, "Yes, I care about you. You can stay in my burrow."

Max was so happy and thanked the rabbit. "You are very kind," said Max. "I am lucky to have a friend like you." From that day on, Max and the rabbit lived together and had many fun adventures.

Once upon a time there was a nice tree. It stood tall and strong in the sunshine.

One day, while the tree was standing there, a little girl who was three years old came walking by. She stopped and looked at the tree with wonder. It was so big and had so many branches!

The little girl wanted to climb the tree, but it seemed too high. Then she had an idea. She ran and got a wooden stool and put it right beside the tree. Then she climbed on and stretched out her hand to the tree's branches. She started climbing, and soon she was up high in the tree!

It was so fun to be up high. The little girl looked down and saw the world looking so small. She looked up and saw the birds flying high in the sky. She felt so free!

The little girl spent a long time up in the nice tree. It was a wonderful afternoon. When she finally got down, she said goodbye to the tree and went off with a happy heart.

Once upon a time there was a fake flower. It felt so real that when you touched it, it seemed like a real flower. Everyone wanted to have a fake flower just like it.

But one day, it vanished. No one knew where it went. Everyone was so sad that the flower was gone.

The next day, something strange happened. The flower reappeared, as if by magic. Everyone was so happy that it was back!

The fake flower seemed to pull a trick and no one knew how it happened. They all touched the flower again, just to make sure it was real. It was still fake, but it still felt real to them.

Everyone was happy that the fake flower was there, whatever the mysterious trick was. They all kept the flower safe, and it stayed with them for a long, long time.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Bella who was turning three. It was her birthday and all of her loved ones were there to celebrate with her. 

Everyone was so excited for her. Her mom brought out a big cake with lots of colourful decorations and candles. "Let's all sing Happy Birthday to Bella," said Bella's mom. Bella laughed with delight!

Bella had the idea to blow out her candles all by herself. She blew with all her might and succeeded in blowing out all the candles. Everyone cheered for her. Then it was time for the most important part of the birthday: tasting the cake! 

Bella's mom carefully cut a big piece of the cake and served it to Bella. She was so independent that she wanted to feed it to herself. She closed her eyes and, when she bit into the soft fluffy cake, it was too delicious! What a special birthday treat. 

From that day on, Bella knew she could do anything she put her mind to, just like she did on her birthday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and watch videos on her tablet. One day, she tried to watch a video but it wouldn't work. She got very upset and said, "I hate this tablet!"

Her mom tried to fix it, but it still wouldn't work. Lily's dad suggested they try watching the video on the TV instead. They found a tube that connected the tablet to the TV and soon the video was playing. Lily was so happy and said, "Wow, that was fast!"

From then on, Lily always used the tube to watch videos on the TV. She never hated her tablet again because she knew there was another way to watch her favorite shows.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tommy. Tommy was three years old and he loved taking pictures. One day, he had a plan. He wanted to take a picture of something beautiful. 

So he decided to go for a walk outside. There were lots of things to see in the park near his home, like the ducks swimming in the pond and the butterflies fluttering past the flowers. 

When Tommy saw the sunset, he had to take a picture. He snapped the perfect shot of the beautiful glowing sky. He was very proud of his work. 

The next day, he showed his picture to his mom and dad. They thought it was wonderful! They hung it up in their living room, so everyone in his family could enjoy the beautiful picture he had taken. 

That made Tommy very happy. He liked making plans and taking pictures to make memories that everyone in his family could enjoy.

Once upon a time, there was a man with a huge axe. He lived in a big forest with many trees. One day, he wanted to make a fire to cook his food. So, he gathered some wood and lit a match. The wood started to burn and the fire grew bigger and bigger. 

Suddenly, the man heard a loud noise. He turned around and saw a huge tree falling down. The tree had been too close to the fire and it burned too much. The man was scared and ran away from the fire. He realized that he needed to be careful when he made a fire in the forest. 

From that day on, the man always made sure to keep his fire far away from the trees. He also learned that he needed to be careful with his huge axe. He knew that if he wasn't careful, he could accidentally burn down the whole forest.

One day, a little girl named Amy was playing in her room. She saw a toy on the floor. The toy was dirty and looked disgusting. Amy thought, "I should clean that toy later."

Amy went to the kitchen and found a yummy cookie. She took a bite and heard a snap. She smiled and ate the whole cookie. Then, she remembered the dirty toy on the floor.

Amy went back to her room and picked up the toy. She took it to the sink and washed it with soap and water. The toy looked clean and nice again. Amy was happy she cleaned the toy and put it back on the shelf.

Molly was so excited. She was finally going on vacation. She looked out the car window. Everything seemed so wide and new. And she was going to explore it all.

When Molly finally arrived, she saw a beach. The ocean was sparkling in the sun. She felt so happy.

After her first day exploring, Molly was tired. She yawned and curled up in her bed. Soon, she was fast asleep.

The next day, Molly went in search of new adventures. She yawned and stretched as she went. Everywhere she looked was amazing. She couldn't believe she was on vacation.

At the end of her vacation, Molly was sad to leave. But she was excited to tell everyone all about her wide adventures.

Once there was a boy called Ryan who was three years old. Ryan had a pet bunny called Flopsy. 
Every day they went to the park together. Ryan liked to pick fruit from the trees. Apples, oranges and plums were Ryan's favourites. 

One day, Ryan saw a bird in the tree. It was a pretty pink bird with a little beak. Ryan wanted to make a new friend, so he reached up to take the fruit from the tree. 

But Flopsy was very helpful and warned Ryan that he could fall from the tree if he went up too high. Ryan listened carefully and decided to hope for the best. He asked the bird if he could have the fruit and it said yes!

So Ryan and Flopsy went home with lots of fruit. Ryan was so happy that he shared the fruit with all his friends. 

Then, every day they all went to the park together to pick more fruit. The bird also came down from the tree to join them, and it became Ryan's new friend. Ryan was very happy and he always hoped for the best!

Once upon a time, in a small hut, there lived a loyal dog named Spot. Spot loved his family very much. He always stayed close to the hut to keep his family safe.

One sunny day, Spot saw a bird outside the hut. The bird said, "Hello, loyal dog! Do you want to play with me?" Spot replied, "Yes, I would love to play, but I must stay near my hut to watch over my family."

The bird understood and said, "That's okay, I can play near the hut too." So, Spot and the bird played together all day long. They had lots of fun and became good friends.

The next day, the bird came back to the hut and asked Spot, "Do you want to play again today?" Spot replied, "Yes, I would love to play with you again." So, they played together near the hut every day, and Spot always kept his family safe.

One day, a boy named Tim found a key. The key was big and shiny. Tim wanted to find what the key could open. He looked all around his tidy room, but there was no lock. Tim was sad.

Tim went to his friend, Sam. Sam had a big seat in his house. Tim and Sam sat on the seat and talked about the key. They wanted to find the lock, too. But they started to fight. Tim wanted to keep the key, but Sam wanted it, too.

In the end, Tim and Sam were so mad that they threw the key out the window. The key was lost in the tall grass. They could not find it again. Tim and Sam were very sad and did not find what the key could open.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to touch things and feel their texture. One day, she saw a famous painting in a museum. The painting had lots of different textures, like rough rocks and soft clouds.

Lily's mom said, "Don't touch the painting, Lily. It's very important and we don't want to damage it." But Lily couldn't resist. She reached out and touched the painting, just for a second.

That night, Lily had a dream. In her dream, the painting came to life and all the textures she had touched started to fight with each other. The rough rocks were pushing the soft clouds away, and the smooth water was trying to cover everything up.

When Lily woke up, she knew she shouldn't have touched the painting. She felt bad for not listening to her mom. But she also learned that sometimes, our dreams can teach us important lessons.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy tools. He had a hammer, a screwdriver, and a saw. One day, Timmy was playing with his tools when his friend Billy came over to play.

"Wow, those tools look fun! Can I play with them?" asked Billy.

"Sure, but be careful. The saw is really sharp and could bite you," warned Timmy.

Billy picked up the saw and tried to use it, but it was too big for him. "This tool doesn't fit me very well," he said.

Timmy laughed and showed him how to use the hammer instead. They played together for hours, building and fixing things with their toy tools. And they never forgot to be careful and watch out for the biting saw.

Once upon a time there was a family who wanted to visit the ocean. They wanted to see the whales, so they packed their bags and went to the beach.

When they arrived, they looked out over the water. Suddenly they saw a big, sleepy whale swimming near the shore. They waved, and the whale waved back! 

The family stayed for a while and watched the whale swim around. Soon it was time to go home, so the family thanked the whale for the visit and gave it a big goodbye.

The family went back home with happy memories of the sleepy whale. They looked forward to visiting again soon!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lola. Lola was three years old and liked to share her toys with her friends. One day, Lola was playing her favourite game, but when her friend Sarah arrived, something weird happened.

Sarah was surprised to see that Lola was not sharing the game with her like she always did. This was very strange! Lola smiled and said, "I have a surprise! I am going to share it with you!" 

Lola gave Sarah a shock. She had something special up her sleeve, and it was a surprise. Sarah was thrilled! She said, "It's so weird! Is it really a surprise?"

Lola smiled and said, "Yes! Let's share it together." Lola and Sarah opened the box and saw something wonderful inside! It was a beautiful, sparkly toy. 

Both girls were overjoyed and shared the toy together. They laughed and hugged each other, celebrating their amazing discovery. From then on, Lola and Sarah shared many more surprises!

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy who had a daughter. The daughter was very happy and loved to play with her toys. One day, the mommy and daddy told the daughter that they were going to take her to the park. The daughter was very excited and couldn't wait to go.

But then, the mommy and daddy had to delay the trip to the park because it started to rain. The daughter was sad because she wanted to go to the park so badly. The mommy and daddy promised that they would take her to the park as soon as the rain stopped.

After a while, the rain stopped and the mommy and daddy took the daughter to the park. But when they got there, they saw something weird. All the swings were missing! The daughter was confused and didn't understand why the swings were gone. The mommy and daddy explained that sometimes things can be weird and unexpected, but they can still have fun and play in other ways. And so, the daughter played on the slide and had a great time at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick daisies. One day, she found a black daisy that she had never seen before. 

Lily picked the black daisy and showed it to her friend, Timmy. "Look, Timmy! I found a black daisy!" she said. 

Timmy looked at the black daisy and said, "Wow, that's so cool! Can I write about it in my journal?" 

Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, you can write about it. I love daisies." 

Timmy wrote about the black daisy in his journal and showed it to Lily. She smiled and said, "That's a great story, Timmy. Thank you for writing about my favorite flower." 

From that day on, Lily and Timmy would often write stories about the black daisy and all the adventures they had together. They were the best of friends and loved to explore the world around them.

Anna and Ben like to play in the park. They have a big sandpit where they can dig and build. One day, they find something shiny in the sand. It is a coin. It is gold.

"Wow, look what we found!" Anna says. "It is so pretty and bright. Maybe it is magic."

"Maybe we can find more," Ben says. "Let's dig deeper and faster. Maybe there is a treasure."

They rush to get their shovels and buckets. They dig and dig and dig. They find more coins. They find rings and necklaces and bracelets. They find a big chest full of gold.

"We are so successful!" Anna says. "We are rich! We can buy anything we want. We can share with our friends and family."

They are very happy and excited. They hug and dance and sing. They do not see the sign that says "Do not dig. Sandpit under construction. Fake gold for decoration."

Once there was a small girl. She had a funny wish - she wanted to add a valley to her garden. She ran to her grandmother and asked her if she could add a valley. Grandmother said no. She said the valley was too big, and it was also very ugly.

So the little girl went outside to look for a valley of her own. But no matter how long she searched, she couldn't find any valley that was just right. 

Then one day, she had an idea. Instead of finding a valley, she could make one! She started working, using her hands and bits of the garden - stones, mud, and little plants. Day after day she worked, and slowly a valley started to grow in her garden.

Finally it was done. When the little girl looked at it, she smiled - her valley was the most beautiful thing in her garden. Grandmother also thought it was beautiful, and they laughed together, and that's how the little girl learned to add a valley to her garden.

Once upon a time there was a kind mommy who had to deliver something important. Mommy was feeling wet from the rain but she still went outside to make the delivery. 

Mommy stepped carefully in the wet puddles, until she came to the door of a nice house. She knocked on the door and a friendly face answered. Mommy handed over the package and the nice person was very happy. 

The rain had made Mommy very wet and soon she got very cold. But soon it was time to go home and be with her family. Mommy was so proud of herself for making the kind delivery and for being brave in the rain.

And so Mommy went home, and soon she was warm and dry again.

Jack and his dad went outside to play. Jack saw a white cone in the grass. He was so excited and he ran to it. Then his dad said, "Let's make it go zip!"

Jack and his dad zipped the white cone up and down the hill. Jack laughed and squealed with joy. He loved the feeling of the wind on his face as they zipped around. His dad was having just as much fun!

When they were done zipping around, they took a break. Jack was thirsty and ate an ice-cream from the white cone. The cool and creamy treat was just what he needed!

Jack and his dad had a great time zipping around on the white cone. They smiled and laughed and had lots of fun. Jack loved every minute of it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. They would run and jump and laugh together. One day, Lily saw a beautiful butterfly flying gracefully in the sky. She wanted to catch it, so she ran after it.

Her friend, Timmy, said, "Lily, stop! You might hurt the butterfly." But Lily didn't listen and kept chasing the butterfly. Suddenly, the butterfly stopped and landed on a flower. Lily slowly walked towards it and gently picked it up. She was so happy to have caught it, but then she realized that it was better to let it go free.

Lily said, "Butterfly, you can go play now. I don't want to hurt you." And with that, she opened her hand and the butterfly flew away. Lily learned that sometimes it's better to stop and be graceful, and that playing with friends is more fun than chasing butterflies.

Once upon a time, there was a seal named Sammy. Sammy lived in the ocean with his seal friends. One day, Sammy found a rough rock on the beach. He showed it to his friends, but they didn't like it. They said it was too rough and not pretty. 

Sammy felt sad that his friends didn't like the rock. He wanted to make them happy. So, he decided to sort through all the rocks on the beach to find a better one. He searched and searched until he found a smooth, shiny rock. 

When he showed it to his friends, they loved it! They said it was beautiful and thanked Sammy for finding it. Sammy learned that it's important to do things to make others happy, even if it takes a little work.

Once upon a time there was a lad named Sam who, although he never said it out loud, often wondered why he felt different from the other children. One day, he was caught off guard when he heard one of his friends say, "You don't look right, Sam!" Feeling uncomfortable, Sam decided to find out what was wrong, so he went to see the doctor. 

When Sam got to the doctor's, the doctor asked him a few questions and scribbled down some notes on a piece of paper. At the end of their meeting, the doctor handed Sam the note and said, "Sam, you may feel different than the others, but that doesn't make you any less special. Your differences are a part of who you are, and you should never be ashamed of them."

Sam thanked the doctor and, as he walked home, he wondered about the doctor's words. He was confused but also felt a little bit better. On the way, he realized that even though he was different from the rest, he still belonged in the world and could be special in his own way. 

This moral story teaches children that everyone is special in their own way and that it is important to be comfortable with their differences, no matter what.

Once upon a time there was a tire that lived in the playground. The tire wanted to go for a ride, but no one was around to help. Then one day, a little boy came to the playground. The tire saw him and asked, "Will you take me for a ride?". The little boy said, "Yes, I will take you for a ride". But when the little boy tried to open the tire, it refused. The tire said, "No! I don't want to go for a ride". So the little boy had to find a different tire to go for a ride. He found an open tire and the two of them went for a really fun ride. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She loved to play and explore. One day, she went outside to play, and as she wandered, she found a secret. It was a shiny thing that sparkled in the sun. She decided to take it home and polish it.

Every day, Lucy polished her secret. She worked hard, but carefully. With every rub, the secret shone brighter and brighter. Soon, it was the shiniest thing in the room. 

One day, Lucy wanted to show someone her secret. But who could she tell? She decided to keep it quiet. She knew that if she said even a word, the secret would not be a secret any more. 

So Lucy kept her secret tucked away, and continued to polish it. Every day she worked hard, but carefully. It shone so brightly that it lit up the room with a beautiful light. 

Lucy and her secret were best friends. And the secret remained a secret.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his triangle blocks. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to pack up his toys and put them away. But Timmy was feeling naughty and didn't want to listen. 

"Timmy, it's time to pack up your toys," said his mom. 

"No, I don't want to," replied Timmy. 

His mom tried to reason with him, but Timmy just wouldn't listen. He kept playing and playing until it was time for bed. 

The next morning, Timmy woke up to find that his favorite triangle block was missing. He searched and searched, but couldn't find it anywhere. It turned out that his dog had chewed it up during the night. Timmy felt sad and wished he had listened to his mom and packed up his toys.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sally. She had a purple pillow that she loved very much. Whenever she was sad or hurt, she would cuddle up with her pillow and think.

One day Sally was feeling very lonely. She thought of how nice it would be to have a friend to play with. She put her head down on her pillow, closed her eyes and thought.

Suddenly, Sally heard a voice from the pillow! It said, "What's wrong Sally? You seem so sad!"

Sally was so surprised she jumped up! She asked, "Who are you?"

The pillow said, "My name is Purple Pillow. I'm here to be your friend!"

Sally smiled. She thought that a purple pillow as a friend was better than nothing. "All right then," she said, "Let's be friends!"

And from that day on, Sally and her purple pillow were best friends. They played and talked and laughed every day. Sally was never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Betsy. Betsy loved to draw with pastels, but her room was always messy. Her mom told her to tidy up before she could draw.

Betsy started to clean up her room, but she was sad because she wanted to draw. Suddenly, her friend Sammy arrived. Sammy also loved to draw, but he had a big box of pastels that he shared with Betsy.

Betsy was happy to see Sammy, but she was also worried because her room was still messy. Sammy noticed and said, "Don't worry about your room, let's draw together!" Betsy was so excited and they drew beautiful pictures together. Betsy realized that sometimes it's okay to have a messy room as long as you have good friends to draw with.

Once upon a time, there was a little otter. The otter was very cute and had gray fur. One day, the otter was swimming in the river when it saw a big fish. The otter wanted to catch the fish, but it didn't understand how to do it.

The otter asked its friends for help, but they didn't know how to catch the fish either. Then, a wise old otter came along and showed the little otter how to catch fish. The little otter was so happy and thanked the wise old otter. From that day on, the little otter understood how to catch fish and was never hungry again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit who was very alert. She was always watching to see what animals were around. One day she was out hopping in the grass when she heard a loud noise. It was a hammer.

"Hello!" she said, "Who is there?"

The hammer answered back.

"It's me," he said. "I am a hammer and I am here to help build something."

The rabbit thought this was a great idea. She crawled over to the hammer to take a closer look.

"What are you making?" she asked.

The hammer replied, "I am building a house for the other animals. We have to work together to get it done in time."

The rabbit was so excited that she started helping the hammer. Together they worked to build the house and soon it was finished. All the animals were so grateful for the new house and they thanked the rabbit and the hammer.

The rabbit was alert and happy that she had been able to help out. She hopped away into the sunset, and all the animals were happy.

Once there were two friends. They liked to match things. In their house, they matched socks and blocks. One day they wanted to match their arms. So they each grabbed one arm and put them together. But one arm was very heavy. It was too heavy to match! The other arm was light and bouncy. The friends had a lot of fun matching it. They bounced it up and down and around. Then they decided to take a rest and have some snacks. They both laughed and had a great time. They always remembered the day they tried to match their arms.

Once there was a bunny who was looking for lots of friends. He looked high and low but couldn't find anyone. Then one day, he saw a friendly carrot. The bunny asked the carrot if he wanted to join together and be friends. The carrot was happy and said yes! So, the bunny and the carrot became best friends. They did everything together. They played tag, went for walks in the meadow and ate yummy carrots. They also helped each other when they were in need. The bunny and the carrot were happy together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain, but her mommy said it was too harsh for her. One day, while Lily was playing, it started to rain really hard. She didn't have an umbrella, so she got all wet. But then, a man with a big smile on his face came by and gave her an umbrella. Lily was so happy! She smiled and thanked the man. From that day on, Lily always brought her umbrella when she wanted to play outside in the rain.

Once there was a mommy and a baby. Mommy decided to go to the store and buy some food. She bought some peppers. They were pink and smelled nice.

When the mommy and baby got home, the baby asked about the peppers. Mommy said, "We can make a yummy snack with the peppers. Do you want to help?" The baby said yes.

Mommy cut the peppers into slices and put them into a pan with some oil. The baby watched as the peppers cooked. When they were done, they were nice and brown.

The mommy and baby sat at the table and talked about how yummy the peppers tasted. They both ate their peppers with a smile on their faces.

The end.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went outside to play. He loved to run and jump and have fun. But today was a little different because it was raining outside. Timmy didn't mind though, he loved to play in the wet rain.

As he was playing, Timmy saw a sign that said "Caution: slippery when wet". But Timmy didn't pay attention to the sign and kept playing. He ran and jumped and had so much fun, until he slipped on the wet ground.

Timmy fell down and hurt himself badly. He realized he should have listened to the sign and been more careful. From that day on, Timmy always paid attention to signs and made sure to be safe when playing outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little man. His name was Joe. He was very worried. He heard about a big volcano that was going to happen. Joe was so worried he decided to go and see it for himself. 

Joe traveled many miles and finally he arrived at the volcano. He saw big chunks of rock flying out of it and smoke coming from the top. Joe was even more worried! 

But then something amazing happened. Joe noticed a rainbow coming out of the volcano. All of Joe's worries disappeared. The rainbow was so beautiful and peaceful. 

Joe hugged the volcano and thanked it for the rainbow. Then he went on his way with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a job, he had to help his mom with the dishes. Timmy didn't like his job, he wanted to play outside. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her with the dishes, but Timmy said no. 

"I want to run and play outside," said Timmy. 

"But Timmy, helping with the dishes is useful," said his mom. 

Timmy didn't listen and ran outside to play. While he was running, he tripped and fell. He hurt his knee really bad and had to go to the hospital. Timmy learned that sometimes it's important to do your job and listen to your mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy wanted to make a picture for his mommy. He needed glue to stick the paper together. Timmy asked his mommy, "Can I have some glue, please?" His mommy said, "Yes, but be careful, glue is sticky." 

Timmy started to make his picture, but he accidentally spilled glue on his hand. "Oh no!" cried Timmy, "I am stuck!" His mommy came to help and said, "Don't worry, we can clean it off." 

After they cleaned the glue off, Timmy finished his picture. It was a picture of a fierce lion. His mommy said, "Wow, that's amazing! I can see the lion's big teeth and sharp claws." Timmy smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, mommy." And they both hugged each other. The end.

One day, a girl named Jane went for a walk in the park. She felt so sleepy that she yawned. She saw some pretty flowers and bright birds. It made her smile. Then she spotted something even better. It was a big plate of candy lying on the ground! Jane was so happy. She quickly grabbed the candy and ran over to a nearby bench. 

Jane shared the candy with a little boy. "Thank you," he said. Jane smiled. She said, "Would you like to play together?" The little boy nodded. They laughed and played in the park. 

As the sun started to set, Jane and the little boy said goodbye. Jane was so tired that she yawned. She was ready to go home. But before she left, Jane looked back and waved goodbye. The little boy waved back, smiling. It was a very pretty day.

John and his Mom were walking near the lake.

"Look, Mom!" John yelled, pointing to the lake. 
"Let's get a raft and go for a ride!" 

Mom smiled. "Ok, let's do it!"

They bought a raft and soon arrived to the lake. Then, Mom and John got on the raft.

"This is fun!" John said. 

Suddenly, the funny raft started to shake.

"What's happening, Mom?" John asked, scared.

"Oh, no," Mom said. "I guess this raft is not so funny anymore. We're sinking!" 

John started to cry. 

But, it was too late. Mom and John fell into the lake and they never came back up.

Once upon a time, there were two brave friends named Ben and Jen. They had one problem, they needed to find a needle. Ben and Jen were very stubborn, so they didn't want to ask anyone for help.

One day they decided they should enter the forest to look for the needle. It was a scary place but they didn't give up. After a few hours, they still had not found the needle.

Suddenly, they heard a squeak! Ben and Jen followed the noise and they spotted a little mouse with a needle in its paws. The mouse wanted to keep the needle so it wouldn't give it to them.

Ben and Jen were determined to get the needle though, so they refused to give up. They were very patient and stayed in front of the mouse for a few hours until it finally gave them the needle.

Ben and Jen went home feeling very proud of themselves. They both had been brave and stubborn and because of that, they had found the needle.

Once upon a time there was a helpful person. They always wanted to help people in need. One day, that helpful person found a strange box with a mixer inside. They thought it would be a good idea to use the mixer to help people.

So, the helpful person took the mixer and made an amazing drink. It was sweet and delicious. Everyone who tasted it said it was the best drink they had ever had. 

The helpful person was so happy to see everyone enjoying the drink that they made with the mixer. Everyone was so thankful to that helpful person for helping them with the special drink. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little hut in the woods. It was very smelly because a big, stinky skunk lived there. The skunk loved to put smelly things in his hut to make it even more smelly.

One day, a little girl named Lily walked by the hut. She smelled the smelly hut and said, "Ew, what a smelly hut!" She wanted to help the skunk make his hut smell better. So, Lily went to find some nice smelling flowers.

Lily found some pretty flowers and put them in the smelly hut. The skunk liked the flowers and said, "Thank you, Lily!" Now, the hut smelled much better. The skunk and Lily became good friends and played together in the woods every day.

Lily loved to splash in the water. She had a new suit that was pink and had flowers on it. She put on her suit and ran to the pool with her mom.

But when she got to the pool, she saw a big sign. It said "Pool Closed". Lily was sad. She wanted to splash and play. She asked her mom why the pool was closed.

Her mom said there was a problem with the water. It was not clean and safe. They had to fix it. Lily did not understand. She was persistent. She said "Please, mom, let me splash. Just a little bit."

Her mom shook her head. She said "No, Lily, we can't. It's not good for you. How about we go to the park instead? There is a fountain there. You can splash in the fountain."

Lily thought for a moment. She liked the fountain. It was shiny and made funny noises. She nodded. She said "Okay, mom, let's go to the fountain. But can I still wear my suit?"

Her mom smiled. She said "Of course, Lily, you can wear your suit. You look very pretty in it. Come on, let's go."

Lily took her mom's hand. They walked to the park. Lily saw the fountain. She ran to it and started to splash. She was happy. She forgot about the pool. She had fun with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a big, noisy whale. He loved to swim and play in the sea. One day, he saw a little fish swimming nearby. The whale wanted to play with the fish, but he didn't know how to be gentle. So he threw the fish into the air and caught it again. The fish felt scared and didn't want to play with the whale anymore.

The whale felt sad when he saw that the fish was scared. He realized that he had been too rough and didn't want to hurt anyone again. From that day on, the whale learned to be gentle and kind to all the sea creatures. He made lots of new friends and they all loved to play together.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and gentle to others, even if we are big and strong. We should always think about how our actions might affect others and try to be gentle with them.

Lily liked to bake with her mom. They made cakes and pies and cookies. Lily liked to eat them too. She liked to lick the spoon and the bowl. Mom said baking was fun and yummy.

One day, Lily wanted to bake with mom, but mom was busy. Mom had to work on her laptop. She said she had a lot of things to do. Lily was sad and bored. She looked for something to do. She saw the hose in the yard. She had an idea.

Lily took the hose and turned it on. She sprayed water everywhere. She sprayed the flowers and the grass and the car. She sprayed the dog and the cat and the bird. She sprayed the window and the door and the wall. She laughed and giggled. She thought it was fun and funny.

But mom did not think it was fun or funny. Mom saw the water and the mess. She heard the dog and the cat and the bird. She saw Lily with the hose. She was angry and upset. She ran outside and took the hose from Lily. She turned it off and scolded Lily. She said Lily was naughty and bad. She said Lily had to clean up and say sorry.

Lily was scared and sorry. She did not mean to make mom angry or upset. She did not mean to make a mess. She just wanted to have fun. She cried and hugged mom. She said she was sorry and she loved mom. Mom hugged Lily back. She said she was sorry too and she loved Lily. She said Lily had to be careful and normal. She said they could bake together later. Lily smiled and nodded. She helped mom clean up. She hoped they could make cookies. She liked cookies.

Once there was a volcano. It was very tall and had fiery lava that bubbled at the top. Every day, the volcano would yell, "Come play with me!" But nobody ever came to the volcano.

One day, a young girl named Grace heard the volcano. She was curious, so she decided to find out what the volcano wanted.

Grace slowly snuk up to the volcano, being careful to stay a safe distance away. To her surprise, the volcano was calm and patient. 

"What do you want?" Grace asked. 

The volcano replied in a deep voice, "I am lonely. Will you play with me?"

Grace smiled. She was excited to make a new friend.

"Yes, I'll play with you! What should we do?" she asked.

The volcano laughed and yelled, "Let's have an adventure!"

Tim and Jen are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. One day, they see a big pan on the stove. It is shiny and round. They want to touch it.

"Come, Jen, let's see what is in the pan," Tim says.

"No, Tim, we should not. Mom said the stove is hot and we can get hurt," Jen says.

But Tim does not listen. He climbs on a chair and reaches for the pan. He does not see the flame under the pan. He grabs the handle and pulls. The pan is very hot. Tim screams and drops the pan. The pan falls on the floor and makes a loud noise. The pan is full of soup. The soup spills everywhere. It is a big mess.

Mom hears the noise and runs to the kitchen. She sees Tim and Jen and the soup and the pan. She is very angry and scared.

"Tim, Jen, what have you done? You could have burned yourself or the house. How could you be so naughty?" Mom says.

Tim and Jen are very ashamed. They know they did a bad thing. They look at Mom and say sorry.

"Sorry, Mom, we were curious. We wanted to see the pan. We did not mean to make a mess," Tim and Jen say.

Mom hugs them and says, "I'm glad you are not hurt, but you have to be careful. The kitchen is not a place to play. You have to listen to me and follow the rules. Do you understand?"

Tim and Jen nod and say, "Yes, Mom, we understand. We will not do it again."

Mom says, "Good. Now help me clean up the soup and the pan. And then we can have some cookies and milk."

Tim and Jen help Mom clean up. They learn their lesson. They are sorry and ashamed, but they are also happy and grateful. They love Mom and Mom loves them.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun. Bun loved to hop around in the fields and play with his friends. One day, Bun saw a wise old owl sitting on a tree branch.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. They also like to eat yogurt. Yogurt is yummy and good for them.

Anna liked to read books. She had many books in her room. She read them every day. She read them on her bed, on her chair, on her floor. She read them with her toys, with her dolls, with her teddy.

One day, Anna wanted to read a new book. She saw it on the shelf. It was big and colorful. It had a picture of a princess on the cover. Anna reached for the book. But it was too high. She could not get it.

She tried to jump. She tried to climb. She tried to use a stool. But nothing worked. She was too small. She felt sad and angry. She wanted the book.

She saw her brother Tom. He was big and tall. He could get the book. She asked him for help.

"Tom, can you please get me that book?" she said.

Tom looked at the book. He looked at Anna. He smiled.

"Sure, I can get you that book," he said. "But what will you give me?"

Anna thought. She did not have much to give. She had her books, her toys, her dolls, her teddy. But she liked them all. She did not want to give them away.

"Nothing," she said. "Just get me the book. It is easy for you."

Tom shook his head.

"No, nothing is not enough," he said. "If you want the book, you have to give me something. How about your mattress? It is soft and comfy. I want it."

Anna gasped.

"My mattress? No, you can't have my mattress!" she said. "That is where I sleep. That is where I read. I need my mattress."

Tom shrugged.

"Then you can't have the book," he said. "It is too bad. It is a nice book. It has a princess and a dragon and a castle. I will read it myself."

He reached for the book. He took it from the shelf. He walked away.

Anna felt tears in her eyes. She wanted the book. She wanted to read it. She wanted to see the princess and the dragon and the castle. She did not want to give up her mattress. She did not know what to do.

She ran after Tom. She grabbed his arm. She pulled the book.

"Give it back! Give it back!" she shouted.

Tom pulled back. He held the book.

"No, it is mine! It is mine!" he shouted.

They tugged and pulled. They yelled and cried. They made a lot of noise.

Their mom heard them. She came to see what was wrong. She saw them fighting over the book. She saw the book tear. She saw the pages fall. She was not happy.

She took the book from them. She scolded them.

"What are you doing? Why are you fighting? Why are you ruining the book?" she said.

Anna and Tom looked down. They felt sorry. They felt ashamed. They told their mom what happened.

Their mom sighed. She hugged them.

"Anna, Tom, you are both wrong," she said. "Books are not for fighting. Books are for sharing. Books are for learning. Books are for enjoying. You should not be greedy or mean. You should be kind and generous. You should help each other and respect each other. Do you understand?"

Anna and Tom nodded. They understood. They said sorry to each other. They said sorry to their mom. They said sorry to the book.

Their mom smiled. She fixed the book. She gave it to them.

"Here, you can both read the book," she said. "But you have to take turns. And you have to be careful. And you have to say thank you."

Anna and Tom said thank you. They took turns. They were careful. They read the book. They saw the princess and the dragon and the castle. They liked the book. They liked each other. They were happy.

"Oh, hello sheep," she said. "I'm so glad you're here."

The sheep happily bleated and the little girl smiled. She decided to spend the whole afternoon playing with her new friend. They ran around and laughed together in the sunshine until it was time for the little girl to go inside.

As she waved goodbye, she shouted out "Bye bye sheep!" The sheep bleated one final time in response. The little girl couldn't stop smiling, knowing that her day outside had been so much fun.
